headline: Chevron and Microsoft agreed a 20-year deal for gas-fired electricity from a new plant built beside a Microsoft data center in West Texas.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered by 2: the deal was announced 22 Jun 2026, over three months ago.
importance_line: West Texas power buyers and Microsoft customers are affected first, as the deal shows big AI sites building their own gas supply, though the plant still needs a final investment decision and the timeline is the companies' own.
summary: Rigzone reports, citing a Chevron statement of 22 Jun 2026, that Chevron and the investment firm Engine No. 1 will supply natural-gas electricity to a Microsoft data center in West Texas for 20 years from a 2.67-gigawatt plant called Project Kilby. The partners expect a final investment decision this year and power from 2028, and say the plant is designed to avoid initially pulling power through the existing grid.
notes: Older news re-dated by EnergyNow on 4 Oct 2026; original blocked, read at Rigzone. Dates and capacity are the companies' statements.
